title: Expected Value of Candidate Decoding
statement: Let $G$ be a regular unique game with label set $\text{Fin}(q)$, choose a candidate subset of labels for each vertex, and fix a default label. Independently decode each vertex by choosing uniformly from its candidate subset if nonempty, and otherwise using the default. The expected value of the resulting labeling in the associated finite unique-game constraint instance equals the average, over vertices and their neighbors, of the edge agreement value obtained by independently averaging over the two endpoint candidate subsets, using the default for any empty subset.
